<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**7** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **28** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4feccc26851b89dcb8f4d78dfab011e73d12c128` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `08f81a0c1d269f60e109f306efab6b0693ba4ce9` — the merge of head `784b1f9f3110eeb99ec43838259df08047bd6dec` into base `4feccc26851b89dcb8f4d78dfab011e73d12c128`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 08f81a0c1d269f60e109f306efab6b0693ba4ce9 && git checkout 08f81a0c1d269f60e109f306efab6b0693ba4ce9
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4feccc26851b89dcb8f4d78dfab011e73d12c128 784b1f9f3110eeb99ec43838259df08047bd6dec && git checkout -B drift-repro 4feccc26851b89dcb8f4d78dfab011e73d12c128 && git merge --no-ff 784b1f9f3110eeb99ec43838259df08047bd6dec

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4feccc26851b89dcb8f4d78dfab011e73d12c128
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `784b1f9f3110eeb99ec43838259df08047bd6dec`
Local-runs: none

**Inputs read.** Card #24822: its body and all 14 comments, through the half-2 dev report `6312414095`, among them the widened claim `6305515833`, the seat call `6305891812` and the landing note `6310089797`. The binding checklist: half 1's reviews `6308267963` ③ and `6309495055` ③ on PR #25048. PR #25094: its body, its 9-file list, and the net diff against merge base `f46ef4d70`, the PR's second `main` merge. The code the hunks cite, read at the head:
- `engine.ts`: `update()`, the static strips and `settleMasterDetailLanding`;
- `rule-validator.ts`: `stripReadonlyFields`, `staticReadonlyInsertSubject`, `isPreservableUnderAudit`;
- `security-plugin.ts`: steps 3.6 and 3.7, and the `honoured` guard;
- the two grant tables' object files, `TENANT_SCOPE_FIELD_DEF`, `matchesFilterCondition`, and driver-sql's `update`.

Nothing was built, tested or re-run. The only script run was the record tool (`record-recognisers --template`, also with `--paths`). The check-runs were read last. Rendered 2026-10-21T09:46Z.

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) RIGHT: the `(caller, organization)` pairs an update can move a row into equal the Layer 0 wall's admitted set, before and after, on every posture, by id and by predicate.**
- **When the engine spares the column.** All of these hold:
  - `opCtx.postHookWriteImageCheck?.judgesOrganization === true` for a non-system context (`engine.ts` :17641);
  - it is read inside the middleware chain's final handler (:17511), on an `opCtx` built fresh at :17308, so no caller and no REST door can supply the seam or the member;
  - `staticReadonlySparesOrganization` (:2453) holds: the insert subject holds the column (so never `sys_`, never `engine-owned` / `append-only` / `better-auth`), and the provenance is not `'author'`.
- **Who sets the member.** Only step 3.7's composition (`security-plugin.ts` :4369), with `tenantParts` non-empty.
- **What that seam judges: every image the engine stores.**
  - By id: the prior row merged with the final payload (`engine.ts` :18548). That is after both strips and before `driver.update` (:18584).
  - By predicate: every row of the D7 read merged with the payload (:18855), before `updateMany` (:18929).
  - The loop refuses an image that names an organization `clearsWall` does not admit, and an emptied one (`security-plugin.ts` :4336–:4337).
- **The payload half, before `next()`.** `suppliedRows.every(clearsWall)` (:4241) and #22278's emptied refusal (:4243) have already refused every supplied value outside the wall, and every emptied one. Both run under the same `tenantParts` condition the member needs.
- **What clears the wall.** `clearsWall` is `matchesFilterCondition` over `{organization_id: A}` or `{organization_id: {$in: set}}`. Its `looseEq` is strict except for Dates, so an array, object or number in the column counts as naming an organization and is refused, never admitted.
- **The one value a spared key can carry unjudged: `undefined`** (in process only; `namesOrganization` and `emptiesOrganization` are both false for it). driver-sql hands the payload to knex, whose update compiler omits undefined keys, so the column keeps its stored value. The change is to reporting only; see (e) P1.
- **By posture:**
  - `single`: no Layer 0, so no member. Unchanged.
  - `isolated`: {A} before and {A} after. Naming A is now stored as sent and not reported.
  - `group`: an explicit re-point on an app object's injected column goes from {the row's own organization} to the membership set, which is the Layer 0 `$in`. Declared-column objects (U2) and hook-written values (#20013) already reached that set.
  - `group` with no active organization: the same set.
  - A crossing operator: its own Layer 0 is `null`, so there is no member unless it acts for a walled delegator. Then `tenantParts` is the delegator's wall alone (ADR-0090 D10), and the re-point is held to it.
- **Paths with no member, unchanged:**
  - step 3.6's check-only seam;
  - a crossing operator on its own behalf (on an update step 3.7 composes nothing for it, because the no-active-organization arm is insert-only);
  - an array payload (the composition needs `insert || !Array.isArray(data)`, :4298–:4302);
  - `isSystem` (the middleware returns at :2453);
  - a context with no `userId` (step 3.7's own gate, :4006);
  - `single`, and a stack without plugin-security.
- **The gates are not weakened.** None is edited:
  - step 2.7's pre-image selection and the engine's scoped prior read (pinned: `r9` answers 404, and the predicate twin leaves `r9` where it was);
  - #19989's falsy-id refusal;
  - the predicate seam judging every matched row (B1-PRED);
  - the `honoured` fail-closed guard (:4564; B2-HON).
- **One shift, stated.** On a walled update of an app object's injected column, #22278's two refusals are now the ONLY thing between an emptied value and storage. Before, the static strip also took a sent `null` / `''`. This is pinned (8 cells) and ablated: under B2-E22278, org 8 turned red, because with the gate off the spare stores the emptied value. That is right, and it makes #22278 load-bearing here.
- **No path found where a caller-chosen `organization_id` reaches storage on UPDATE without a wall verdict.**

**(b) RIGHT: `judgesOrganization` is set only on step 3.7's composed seam, for an insert or a non-array update, with `tenantParts` non-empty.**
- **One assignment outside tests** (`security-plugin.ts` :4369–:4372; `git grep` at the head). The engine only reads it (:16146 for insert, :17642 for update).
- **Never set on:**
  - step 3.6's `newWriteImageCheck()` seams (:3826, installed at :3839 and :3909). They carry no member, and the composition wraps them in a new object without mutating them;
  - the crossing operator's seam, where `tenantParts` is empty and the spread is `{}`;
  - an array update. The composition is skipped, and the spread restates the condition, so B2-ARR2 is an equivalent mutant, as the body says;
  - `isSystem`, which never reaches step 3.6 or 3.7.
- **The `operation === 'insert'` conjunct was replaced deliberately, not deleted** (half 1's ③1). `tenantParts` is not reassigned after the composition.
- **`sys_` seams.** The member IS now set on a walled `sys_` update seam. The engine's spare ignores it there through the insert-subject condition, so it has no effect (pinned: the sec `sys_` cell; B1-SYS).

**(c) RIGHT: the shared helper, and the descriptor member that travels through `settleMasterDetailLanding`.**
- **`staticReadonlySparesOrganization` (:2453)** is half 1's `insertStaticReadonlySubject` body factored out: the flag, the insert subject holding the column, and the provenance not `'author'`. `insertStaticReadonlySubject` (:2469) behaves identically, because `staticReadonlyInsertSubject` is pure. B1-F4 turns half 1's insert F4 pins red through the shared helper.
- **`updateStaticReadonlySubject` (:2495)** returns the schema object itself when it does not spare, so every unspared update is byte-identical. Otherwise it returns `{name, fields}` without the column. `stripReadonlyFields` reads only `fields` and `name` (`rule-validator.ts` :2117), so the reduced view changes the column and nothing else.
- **One read, one view** (:17641–:17643), feeding:
  - the hide pass (:17652);
  - the by-id strip (:18489);
  - the predicate strip (:18778);
  - through the descriptor, `staticReadonlyStoredView` (:4283).

  No other static-`readonly` update pass reads the column off `updateSchema`. `validate()` is untouched, so its preview stays wall-blind, as stated.
- **`settleMasterDetailLanding` (:10334, not edited): right.**
  - It destructures `staticStrip` and passes that same object to `staticReadonlyStripTakes` (:10359), so the member travels at runtime.
  - It is behaviour-neutral there. That call asks only about the master-detail FK, and the flag moves only `organization_id`. The platform's injected column is a `lookup`, never the master-detail FK, and an authored one has `'author'` provenance and is never spared.
  - The `judgeFkLock` closures read the update's own descriptor.
  - N-c below is a typing nit on this point.

**(d) RIGHT: the pins cover the ruled matrix, and the negative pins are ablation-verified per the PR body.**
- **organizations, real stack, 43 cases:**
  - `group`: C by id and by predicate (stored, shown to `beforeUpdate`, unreported, the seam judged C); D refused; strict; the row's own organization; no active organization, C and D;
  - the declared-column control; the step 2.7 out-of-scope row; the #19989 falsy id;
  - `isolated`: A, and another organization;
  - #22278: 8 cells;
  - the array payload; F4 by id and by predicate;
  - 16 no-wall cells: `single`, `single` with a check, security absent under both postures, the operator crossing under both postures, strict, tenancy-disabled, `preserveAudit`, system;
  - the preview.
- **plugin-security, 16 cases:**
  - SET, UNSET or NO SEAM for each seam, the composed check, the array payload and the system context;
  - a `sys_` object and both grant tables;
  - the delegated update: `group` C and D, and `isolated`.
- **objectql, 23 cases:**
  - SET by id and by predicate; only `organization_id` spared; strict; `readonlyWhen`;
  - an authored column, `sys_` and `engine-owned`;
  - NOT SET in 3 modes × 4 cells, `preserveAudit` included;
  - system; `validate()`.
- **Ablations.**
  - Negative pins: B1-A4u (14/2/12), B2-SET1b, B1-SYS, B1-F4, B2-ARR1, B2-E22278, B2-WALL, B2-PRE27 and B2-PRE27P, B1-PRED, B1-PA2, B1-VIEW, B1-HIDE, B2-HON.
  - Positive controls: B1-A6u and B2-SETOFF.
  - The counts agree with the cells. For example, B1-A4u's org 14 is the 15 no-wall cells less the tenancy-disabled authored column, which the provenance rule keeps.
- **Gaps, non-blocking:**
  - The boundary table's `managedBy: 'system-data'` non-`sys_` app-object row is a probe, not a pin. Parity with insert holds through the shared helper.
  - The grant-table cells are controls that no mutation of the spare can reach, as stated.

**(e) RIGHT: every public-surface change is listed in the changeset and the PR body, N2 included.**
- **Listed:**
  - the published member's contract now covers single-payload updates (no new member; reached through `OperationContext`);
  - the re-point stored as sent, by id and by predicate;
  - no `droppedFields`, no `onFieldsDropped`, no WARN;
  - strict stores;
  - `beforeUpdate` sees the value;
  - no active organization;
  - on-behalf-of;
  - N2: an organization-scoped unique key, a rule, `readonlyWhen` / `requiredWhen`, and hooks;
  - the unchanged list.
- **Precision notes, not missing surface:**
  - **P1.** In process only, an `organization_id: undefined` on a walled update was taken, reported and refused under strict. It is now kept, not reported and not refused, and the stored value is unchanged (knex omits it). There is no REST reach, because JSON carries no `undefined`. Half 1 listed its analogue (F3); this one is not listed.
  - **P2.** `afterUpdate`, `data.record.updated` and every event consumer now see the row in its new organization. The changeset's "outcomes that read the stored organization" sentence covers this, but does not name them.

### ② Semver level

- **`@objectstack/objectql` `minor`: RIGHT.** No member is added. But the published member's contract widens to updates, and an in-process strict update naming an admitted organization is now stored. `Clause-②: yes` owes at least minor, as half 1 did.
- **`@objectstack/plugin-security` `patch`: RIGHT.** The changes are a private type's doc and the plugin's own seam composition.
- **`@objectstack/organizations`: tests only, so no changeset is owed.** All three packages are in the `fixed` group, and none is private.
- **Version skew is inert both ways.** An older engine ignores the member on an update; an older plugin never sets it there.
- **The `Clause-②` line: RIGHT.** `yes (widening)` stands at line start in the PR body and the changeset, as the same sentence. The engine's own gates refuse nothing they accepted before. N2's stored-state refusals (for example, an organization-scoped unique key in the new organization) are the ones a declared-column object already meets, so half 1's reading of N2 (not a narrowing) holds unchanged. `Check Changeset` is green.
- **Tier: RIGHT.** Read on the 8 source paths, `record-recognisers --paths` decides no schema or rules face. The changeset's `Clause-②` line then decides the declaration face, served at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ③ Boundary flags

**The seat's rulings for half 2:**
1. **The spare covers exactly the objects the insert spare covers:** RIGHT. It is the same helper; `sys_` and the platform-internal buckets are excluded (B1-SYS).
2. **#22278, an emptied organization stays refused:** RIGHT. Both halves are untouched, with 8 pins and B2-E22278.
3. **No spare on an array update payload:** RIGHT. The composition is skipped and the spread restates the condition (B2-ARR1).
4. **The gates are kept** (#19989, step 2.7, every matched row, `honoured`): RIGHT. None is edited (B2-PRE27 and B2-PRE27P, B1-PRED, B2-HON).
5. **`preserveAudit` does not widen:** RIGHT. `isPreservableUnderAudit` is untouched, and the injected column is `system: true`, so it is not preservable (B1-PA2).
6. **The "effectively immutable" comment is rewritten:** RIGHT. Step 3.7's paragraph (:3940) now states the stored re-point. The `WriteImageCheckSeam` doc and the removal test's header are rewritten too.
7. **The update preview's behaviour is stated:** RIGHT. It is in the changeset, in the PR body's Acceptance notes, and in the org and oql pins. #25062 carries it.

**`6308267963` ③, what half 2 must not regress:**
1. The setter stays on non-empty `tenantParts`, never on step 3.6's seam or the crossing seam, and the conjunct is replaced deliberately: HELD (:4369).
2. No spare on an array update: HELD.
3. #22278, and the payload half's refusal of D: HELD (:4241, :4243; B2-WALL 16/7/0).
4. One read for the by-id and predicate seams; `isSystem` and update-mode `validate()` unchanged; the census row: HELD (:17641; three census rows).
5. The `honoured` guard: HELD (untouched).
6. The comment: HELD.

**`6309495055` ③, what half 2 must not regress:**
1. The member only on step 3.7's composed by-id or predicate seam; never on step 3.6's update seam, an array payload or `isSystem`: HELD.
2. #22278, without F3 carried across: HELD.
3. F4: HELD.
4. `sys_` objects measured and ruled: HELD. U3 was measured, ruling 1 applies, and the spare's insert-subject condition keeps every `sys_` object's strip.
5. The gates: HELD.
6. `preserveAudit`: HELD.
7. One helper, and the preview: HELD.

**U3, the grant tables: this PR changes nothing for them.**
- `sys_user_position` and `sys_user_permission_set` declare `organization_id` as a plain `Field.lookup` with no `readonly`. So no static strip ever took a re-point there, before or after.
- The spare's insert-subject condition is false for every `sys_` object, so even a read-only column there would keep its strip.
- The only change: step 3.7 now sets the member on their walled update seam, and nothing reads it there.
- A member's re-point still meets the RBAC administration gate (403). An administrator's still meets the wall and the grant's own guards.
- They are pinned as controls, and the before-run with `main`'s sources passes them.

**The dev's flags:**
- **`open_questions`:** none.
- **Stray `/final2.pid` at the filesystem root.** The harness refused its removal. It is outside the repo and the diff. ESCALATED to the seat to delete; not a contract item.
- **`settleMasterDetailLanding` not edited:** right, judged in ①(c).
- **The prose-only edit to `tenant-wall-organization-removal.test.ts`:** inside the claim's test surface.
- **The two no-op ablation attempts, re-run:** fine.
- **`main` not merged a third time: right.** `main` is now `28c9a2cb6`. Its new commits (#25045 spec and driver-turso, #25064 PM tooling, #25080 driver-sql, #25081 platform-objects, #25076 service-messaging) share no file with the 9 paths.
- **Claim surface.**
  - Every `engine.ts` hunk sits in a claimed region: the helpers beside `insertStaticReadonlySubject`, the interface doc, the stored-view helpers, the update hook view, and the by-id and predicate strips.
  - No hunk falls in a fence: #25072 (~:4628, ~:6102–:6251), #24893 (~:91, :9043, :12187), or #25066's `security-plugin.ts` region (~:9133–:9422).
  - `packages/spec`, Middleware A and `tenantLayer0Verdict` are untouched.
- **`Fixes #24822`:** this is the card's last half. The guards "The card this PR closes must claim this branch" and "Part-of PR must not also close its card" are green.

**The dev's out-of-scope findings:**
- **An array update payload beside `where.id`** fails with a raw SQL error (`no such column: 0`), before and after, in process, with nothing stored. Not a boundary item. For the seat to weigh: it is an unenveloped driver error with no carrier.
- **`sys_` objects keep the silent update strip** under ruling 1. Noted.
- **Half 1's N1, the insert-side stale prose,** is unchanged: step 3.7's D2 arm ("the column is read-only to a session payload") and the operator arm ("strips the column from a session payload"). For the seat.

**Notes. None blocks.**

- **N-b:** P2 in ①(e), event consumers covered only by the general sentence.
- **N-c:** `settleMasterDetailLanding`'s declared `staticStrip` type omits the optional member, so the type does not document that it travels. A future rebuild of the descriptor there would drop the member silently. That is harmless for the FK question it asks.

ACCEPT · #24822 half 2 (UPDATE, the last half) · `domain:services` seat 2 · `os-support-ai` · `session_01UmqzD97e14iws6hmVhgZ5y` · 2026-10-21T09:47Z · head `784b1f9f31`.
- This is the review of record for the claim `6305515833`, widened in place for half 2.
- Contract review: owed on the declaration face (`Clause-②: yes`). **PASS** at `TIER_DEFAULT` on this same head (`6312988749`, an isolated reviewer, `Local-runs: none`). It judged every point of half 1's two "must not regress" lists (`6308267963` ③, `6309495055` ③) and the seat's seven half-2 rulings as HELD.

1. **Form:**
   - The first line is `Fixes #24822`. This is the card's last half; half 1 landed as `2b1382a5b3`. The seat's grep finds no other closing keyword beside an issue number.
   - `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is at line start in the body and in the changeset: `@objectstack/objectql` `minor`, `@objectstack/plugin-security` `patch`.

2. **Premise and fix:**
   - Under `group`, an `organization_id` re-point the Layer 0 wall admits is stored as sent, by id and by predicate. One it refuses stays refused. ⛔ Never silently replaced.

3. **Gates:**

   - Every skip is on the roster in `scripts/pm/check-expected-skips.mjs`: Temporal Conformance, the Dogfood Regression Gate matrix, Console Pin Gate, Dogfood Verify CLI, Build Docs, Packed-tarball smoke and the 18.x upgrade harness.
   - Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Build Core, all six Test Core shards, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check Changeset and the closing-target guards are `success`. `mergeable_state` is clean.
   - **Local:** 76 derived, 76 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED.
     - `objectql` 458 files / 8610 passed;
     - `plugin-security` 205 / 4193;
     - `organizations` 15 / 233;
     - three typechecks with `check:test-typecheck` OK, and no debt signature.
4. **Accepted deviations:**

   - A prose-only header edit in `tenant-wall-organization-removal.test.ts`.
